request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: [Name], [Age]-year-old female

Admission Date: [Date]
Discharge Date: [Date]

Chief Complaint:
Left supraclavicular and axillary painful lump

Hospital Course and Treatment:
The patient was admitted to the Hematologic Clinic with a painful left supraclavicular and axillary lump. She had received the first dose of the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine five days prior to presentation. The patient experienced injection site pain, headaches, chills, and a sense of “heaviness” of the neck and upper chest for two days after injection that gradually resolved. On physical examination and Doppler ultrasound, multiple enlarged lymph nodes were seen in the axillary, supraclavicular, and low lateral neck areas. Painful axillary lymphadenopathy also appeared after the second dose of the vaccine. No other abnormal findings were noted. Blood tests including full chemistry, blood count, and CRP levels were within normal limits. The patient was treated with pain relief medication and her symptoms improved gradually until complete resolution.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient responded well to pain relief medication and her symptoms gradually resolved over time. No complications were reported during hospitalization.

Follow-Up Plan:
The patient will be discharged with instructions to follow up with her primary care physician for any concerns or symptoms in the future. No further follow-up is required at this time.

Summary:
This is a case of a healthy middle-aged woman who presented with an adverse reaction to the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine resulting in painful axillary lymphadenopathy. The patient was treated with pain relief medication, and her symptoms resolved over time with no complications identified during hospitalization. The patient will be discharged with instructions to follow up with her primary care physician for any concerns or symptoms in the future.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: R59**

**Why this is the principal diagnosis**
- After investigation, the condition chiefly responsible for the admission was painful localised lymphadenopathy (axillary, supraclavicular, low lateral neck). It was attributed to an adverse reaction to the Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine.
- Under the ICD-10-AM/ACS convention for adverse effects of a correctly prescribed and administered drug or vaccine, the principal diagnosis is the nature of the effect, the manifestation.
- The workup (Doppler ultrasound, full bloods, CRP) found no other underlying cause, such as infection or malignancy. That leaves the lymphadenopathy itself as the condition chiefly responsible for the episode.
- I chose R59 (enlarged lymph nodes) over L04 (acute lymphadenitis) because the documentation describes enlarged, reactive nodes. It does not document lymphadenitis or infection, and CRP was normal.
- I did not use T88.1 (other complications following immunisation NEC) as principal. The manifestation is specifically documented and classifiable, so the T-code is not preferred.

**Secondary codes**
- **Y59.0** (viral vaccines) should be added as the external cause code identifying the vaccine as the source of the adverse effect.
- **Y92.22** (health service area, as place of occurrence) may also apply, following local practice.

**Coding notes**
- At four characters, the principal diagnosis would likely be **R59.0** (localised enlarged lymph nodes). The involvement is regional, on the left side only, rather than generalised. The three-character category requested is R59.
- The diagnosis section of the summary was withheld. If it documents something different, such as "post-vaccination lymphadenitis," the code choice should be reviewed or clarified with the treating clinician.
